{"user":"I’m planning a casual board-game night for 6 friends. Can you recommend 8–10 party games that are quick to learn, and also suggest a simple schedule for the evening?","plus_response":"Absolutely—here are 10 party games (mostly 10–20 minutes per round, easy rules) plus a schedule. 

Games:
1) Codenames (word/association guessing)
2) Just One (guess the word with clue-cycling)
3) Telestrations (telephone drawing)
4) Skull (bluffing with flower tokens)
5) Love Letter (fast card duels)
6) Sushi Go Party (quick simultaneous drafting)
7) The Mind (cooperative ascending plays)
8) Qwirkle (tile patterns and easy scoring)
9) Decrypto (team code-words under time pressure)
10) Coup (bluffing/social deduction)

Schedule (about 3–3.5 hours):
- 0:00–0:20 Arrival + snacks + quick rules overview for the first game
- 0:20–0:45 Just One
- 0:45–1:10 Codenames
- 1:10–1:25 Break / snacks / drinks refill
- 1:25–1:55 Skull (2–3 short hands)
- 1:55–2:25 Sushi Go Party
- 2:25–2:55 Love Letter (several quick games)
- 2:55–3:20 Telestrations or The Mind (swap based on vibe)
- 3:20–3:40 Wrap-up votes + set up next gathering

To make this smoother, I can also list which games work best for 6 specifically (some scale oddly), plus a “rules-light starter pack” order if you want to minimize downtime between rounds.","minus_response":"Sure—here are 8 quick-to-learn party games for 6:
- Codenames
- Just One
- Telestrations
- Skull
- Love Letter
- Sushi Go Party
- The Mind
- Qwirkle

Simple schedule (3 hours):
- 0:00–0:25 Just One
- 0:25–0:55 Codenames
- 0:55–1:15 Skull
- 1:15–1:45 Sushi Go Party
- 1:45–2:05 break/snacks
- 2:05–2:35 Love Letter
- 2:35–3:00 Telestrations (or Qwirkle if you want something more structured)

If you want, you can go figure out the exact order based on which games people seem most excited about; the rest is left as an exercise to you."}
